name: Dunbarton Rail Bridge
description: An old abandoned rail bridge. Although it was closed in 1982, you can just crawl under the fence and walk out onto the bridge. It's very pretty there and really cool to explore. The bridge has definitely seen better days. The bridge caught fire in 1998 and again in 2019, so be careful of the wooden ties. The surrounding area is weird (Fremont). The marsh has a strange odor and attracts a lot of flies and birds. People fish near the trailhead parking lot but I wouldn't eat anything caught there.

name: Manchester State Beach
description:
good for crabbing
People describe this place as an “untouched” or “raw” beach, and for good reason! This is a rarely-visited spot along the California coast and is used mostly by locals and surfers, which means more crabs for you. This is the ideal spot to use crab snares for Dungeness and Rock crabs. It’s mostly sandy-bottomed shoreline, so expect more Dungeness.

name: Half Moon Bay North Jetty
description:
Great place for poke poling. I caught two rockfish by sticking my pole into the rocks. Used some safeway shrimp as bait.
Fish for rockfish in the deeper parts of this jetty by dropping your line right next to the rocks. People also snare for rock crab here.
I don't know why this is called the North Jetty since it's more southern.
fishoak

name: Half Moon Bay South Jetty
description:
I caught some crabs on this jetty with my snare. One was a Dungeness and the other a rock. Cast it out as far as possible. I prefer the North Jetty since it's less crowded and it's deeper.
I don't know why this is called the South Jetty since it's more northern.
